items.question:
A hospital system's governance committee is evaluating a vendor's AI tool for supporting discharge planning decisions for elderly patients with complex comorbidities. Committee members are debating which safeguards are non-negotiable before approval can be granted.

Which TWO safeguards are non-negotiable governance requirements before deployment? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A defined human decision-maker who retains authority to override the AI recommendation for every individual discharge planning decision.
options.B: A retrospective pilot study comparing AI discharge recommendations against historical decisions to assess alignment with past clinical practice.
options.C: A disclosure mechanism so patients and families understand that AI is contributing to the discharge planning process.
options.D: Full integration with the hospital's electronic health record system to ensure the AI has access to complete, current patient data.
options.E: A vendor attestation that the tool has been trained on a dataset of at least 100,000 elderly patient discharge cases.

items.question:
An enterprise HR team is preparing to deploy an AI tool that will generate promotion recommendations for 5,000 employees across 14 countries. A senior people analyst is tasked with identifying the two governance requirements that must be met before any employee receives an AI-generated recommendation.

Which TWO requirements are non-negotiable before deployment? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The tool must integrate with the performance management system to eliminate manual data entry errors during the recommendation generation process.
options.B: The AI recommendations must be tested for differential impact across gender, ethnicity, disability status, and geographic cohorts before any employee is exposed to an output.
options.C: The tool must generate a written natural-language rationale for each recommendation so that managers understand what factors drove the AI output.
options.D: A named accountable person — not the AI system — must be the owner of each final promotion decision, with genuine authority to override the recommendation.
options.E: The vendor must supply a data-processing impact assessment confirming that training data from EU-based employees was handled under appropriate legal mechanisms.

items.question:
A financial services firm is drafting disclosure language to include in customer communications that were materially shaped by AI. The compliance team is debating which two elements are essential for the disclosure to meet the transparency standard applicable to consequential customer communications.

Which TWO elements are essential? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A plain-language statement that AI was used in generating or informing the content, so recipients know AI was materially involved.
options.B: The specific name and version of the AI model used to generate the communication.
options.C: The name and title of the employee who reviewed the AI output before the communication was sent.
options.D: An indication of any relevant limitations — for instance, whether the content reflects the customer's specific circumstances or provides only general guidance.
options.E: A hyperlink to the firm's complete AI governance policy document for customers who wish to review the firm's AI use principles.

items.question:
A healthcare group is deploying an AI system that reads patient records to generate personalised appointment reminders and care instructions. The privacy team is reviewing the patient consent process and must identify the two elements without which the consent process would be inadequate.

Which TWO elements are essential for an adequate consent process? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Patients must be offered an opt-in choice before the system reads any patient record, regardless of the communication's clinical urgency.
options.B: Patients must be clearly informed, before they encounter the AI system, that it will access their health records to generate communications — stated in plain language.
options.C: Patients must have a clear, accessible mechanism to opt out of AI-generated communications and receive human-generated alternatives instead.
options.D: Patients must be shown a representative sample of AI-generated communications before they consent, so they know what style and format to expect.
options.E: The AI system must be validated using synthetic patient records before any real patient data is accessed to generate communications.

items.question:
A regional hospital has completed procurement of an AI diagnostic support tool for its radiology department. The following steps have been completed: vendor contract signed with appropriate data-processing terms; IT infrastructure confirmed as compatible; vendor has delivered training documentation and conducted two information sessions with radiology staff. The chief medical information officer (CMIO) must now decide the NEXT step before the tool is used in active patient care.

What should the CMIO do NEXT?

options.A: Deploy the tool across the full radiology department immediately, so radiologists can begin generating real-world performance data under live clinical conditions.
options.B: Schedule additional vendor demonstrations for radiologists who remain sceptical, to ensure staff buy-in before any clinical use begins.
options.C: Complete and publish the departmental AI governance policy covering escalation procedures and radiologist override obligations before any tool use.
options.D: Conduct a supervised validation phase in which radiologists use the tool alongside their standard independent assessments for a defined period, comparing outputs before any AI recommendation influences a final report.

items.question:
After deploying Claude to generate client proposal documents, a SaaS company is told its AI use policy must include 'AI disclosure.' An account manager adds a paragraph to each proposal explaining that the document uses a transformer-based language model validated through chain-of-thought prompting. A compliance reviewer flags this as unnecessary.

What distinction is the compliance reviewer MOST likely making?

options.A: Disclosure requires stating that AI was used and in what capacity; it does not require a technical explanation of the model's architecture or methodology.
options.B: The technical explanation is accurate but exceeds the standard word count for compliant disclosure language.
options.C: Disclosure is only required for proposals sent to regulated-industry clients; standard B2B software proposals are exempt.
options.D: The manager should have used a disclaimer rather than a disclosure, as the two carry different legal weight.

items.question:
A paralegal at a mid-sized property firm uses Claude to prepare two types of client communications. The first summarises publicly available case law on standard lease renewal provisions for a client information sheet. The second recommends specific protective clauses the firm's current tenant client should insist on including in their upcoming commercial lease.

Which output is legal advice requiring a supervising solicitor's authority before issue?

options.A: The first output, because case law summaries carry legal authority and must be reviewed by a qualified solicitor before client distribution.
options.B: The second output, because recommending specific contract language for a particular client's circumstances is a legal judgment, not a general information summary.
options.C: Both outputs, because any communication produced by a law firm on legal matters is legal advice regardless of its content.
options.D: Neither output, because both are based on existing legal sources and do not constitute original legal analysis.

items.question:
A startup's AI-assisted hiring tool produces a shortlist that later reveals systematic exclusion of candidates over age 50. When the board questions the CEO, the CEO says the vendor's indemnity clause transfers liability for discriminatory AI outcomes to the vendor, so the startup bears no accountability.

What is MOST likely incorrect about the CEO's position?

options.A: Employment discrimination indemnity clauses are generally unenforceable, so the startup faces full legal liability regardless of the vendor agreement.
options.B: The board, not the CEO, is the appropriate body to determine how accountability is allocated between the startup and the vendor.
options.C: Legal liability and accountability are distinct concepts — a vendor indemnity may limit financial liability, but it cannot remove the startup's accountability for its decision to deploy and use the tool on real candidates.
options.D: The vendor's indemnity clause would be superseded by applicable employment discrimination legislation in most jurisdictions.

items.question:
An energy company designates a field safety officer as the human reviewer for AI-generated maintenance schedules. Each schedule covers 12 pieces of equipment. Audit data shows the officer approves 97% of AI recommendations with an average review time of 34 seconds per schedule. An internal auditor flags this pattern in their quarterly report.

What is the auditor MOST likely concerned about?

options.A: The 97% approval rate is statistically implausible for a tool with known false-positive rates, suggesting the data is being recorded incorrectly.
options.B: A 34-second review period suggests the officer is processing schedules efficiently and may simply have high confidence in the AI tool's accuracy.
options.C: The AI tool's maintenance recommendations should be cross-referenced against a second independent system before human review is conducted.
options.D: A 34-second review of a 12-equipment maintenance schedule is insufficient time to substantively assess the recommendations; the oversight step appears nominal rather than genuine.

items.question:
A pharmaceutical company's consumer information line uses Claude for two types of responses. First: a caller asks what the maximum daily dose is for a specific over-the-counter painkiller; Claude provides the labelled dosage from the product monograph. Second: a caller asks whether they can safely take that painkiller alongside their prescribed anticoagulant; Claude responds that the combination is generally safe for most people at standard doses.

Which response crosses into medical advice requiring clinical review?

options.A: The second response, because advising a specific caller on a drug interaction involving their prescribed medication is clinical guidance, not general product information.
options.B: The first response, because dosage information should only be communicated to consumers by a registered pharmacist.
options.C: Both responses, because any AI output on a medical information line constitutes regulated medical advice regardless of content.
options.D: Neither response, because both are derived from labelled product information and do not involve a clinical diagnosis.

items.question:
A retail group's HR director argues their AI recruitment tool cannot be unfair because it was trained on five years of the company's own hiring records and consistently produces outcomes that match their historical hiring patterns. A data ethics specialist challenges this reasoning.

Why is the data ethics specialist MOST likely correct?

options.A: Industry benchmark data carries copyright restrictions, and using proprietary internal hiring records to train an AI model requires explicit data licencing.
options.B: Historical hiring patterns that produced skewed demographic outcomes can embed existing bias — consistency with the past is not evidence of fairness; it may be evidence of bias perpetuation.
options.C: A model trained exclusively on internal data cannot pass external fairness audits because it lacks exposure to industry-wide hiring diversity benchmarks.
options.D: The five-year training window is too short to account for demographic shifts in the labour market, making the model statistically unreliable.

items.question:
A non-profit uses Claude to categorise and draft initial responses to donor correspondence. The executive director says donors were adequately notified because the organisation mentioned in its last annual report that it was 'exploring AI tools to improve efficiency.' A privacy officer raises a concern.

What is the privacy officer MOST likely identifying?

options.A: Annual reports are not legally binding notification documents; a dedicated consent form is required for each donor before AI processing begins.
options.B: Donors should have been given an explicit opt-in choice before AI was used to process their correspondence, not merely mentioned in a general publication.
options.C: A general mention of 'exploring AI tools' in an annual report does not constitute adequate notice that AI is actively processing individual donor correspondence; notice must be specific to the purpose and the actual processing being carried out.
options.D: Donor correspondence qualifies as sensitive personal data, requiring a data protection impact assessment before any AI processing begins.

items.question:
A bank is responding to a regulatory inquiry asking it to describe both its AI oversight controls and its AI transparency measures for its automated lending model. A junior compliance team member suggests that disclosing the model's decision criteria to loan applicants addresses both requirements in a single document.

Why is the junior team member's suggestion MOST likely inadequate?

options.A: Transparency obligations are satisfied by providing applicants with a summary of model performance statistics, not by disclosing decision criteria.
options.B: Oversight controls and transparency measures address the same governance obligation, so a single document does satisfy both requirements.
options.C: Disclosing decision criteria to applicants could expose commercially sensitive model information, making this approach legally risky.
options.D: Oversight controls refer to internal governance mechanisms — review structures, human authority over decisions, escalation paths — while transparency measures concern informing affected individuals. Criterion disclosure satisfies the second requirement but says nothing about whether the first is in place.

items.question:
A journalist at a media company uses their company-issued laptop to ask Claude to draft several LinkedIn posts about their personal freelance photography business during their lunch break. The company's IT policy states that Claude use on company devices is 'permitted for journalism and editorial work.' HR asks whether an acceptable-use violation occurred.

What is the BEST assessment?

options.A: This is an acceptable-use violation — 'permitted for journalism and editorial work' does not extend to personal commercial activity, regardless of the time of day it occurred.
options.B: Personal use of company software during the employee's own lunch hour is generally permissible and does not constitute a policy violation.
options.C: The primary concern is that AI-generated LinkedIn content could be detected and damage the journalist's personal professional reputation.
options.D: This is a data security concern — personal business information the employee entered into Claude may be retained by the vendor beyond the company's data governance controls.

items.question:
A logistics company's operations manager says: 'The AI allocates routes for our 200 daily deliveries; I just confirm each morning that the system ran without errors.' When a carrier challenges an allocation that increased their route load by 40%, asking who made the decision, the manager responds: 'The system made it.'

What governance problem does the manager's position MOST directly illustrate?

options.A: The operations manager is not qualified to oversee an automated decision system that materially affects carrier contract terms.
options.B: Treating the AI as the decision-maker removes a named human from accountability for a consequential business decision; the manager's role should be substantive oversight, not error-checking.
options.C: Route allocations are operational rather than consequential decisions, so the governance concern is lower than the scenario implies.
options.D: The carrier's complaint reveals an audit trail gap — the system should log which specific inputs caused the 40% load increase.

items.question:
A retail bank uses a third-party AI credit-scoring model integrated into its systems by a technology vendor. A bank analyst inputs customer data and issues credit decisions based on the AI score. A customer is incorrectly denied a mortgage due to a scoring error traced to a data normalisation bug introduced during the integration. The customer challenges the denial.

What is the MOST accurate characterisation of where primary accountability to the customer lies?

options.A: Accountability rests entirely with the AI model vendor, because the scoring error originated in the model's data requirements.
options.B: Accountability rests entirely with the integration technology vendor, because the data normalisation bug was their deliverable.
options.C: The bank bears primary accountability to the customer as the decision-making entity; how that accountability is distributed between the model vendor and integration vendor is an internal commercial matter.
options.D: Accountability is shared equally and symmetrically between the model vendor, the technology vendor, and the bank, because all three contributed to the error.

items.question:
A pharmaceutical company deploys an AI patient-matching tool for clinical trial recruitment. The vendor assures the procurement team the model was 'fully debiased through adversarial retraining on demographic variables.' A post-deployment review by the biostatistics team finds the model still under-represents certain ethnic groups relative to disease prevalence in the relevant population.

What is the MOST likely explanation for the persistent disparity?

options.A: The vendor's adversarial retraining was incorrectly implemented and the model should be returned for re-training under the company's direct oversight.
options.B: The biostatistics team used a different fairness metric than the vendor's debiasing process targeted, and the discrepancy reflects different but equally valid fairness definitions.
options.C: Clinical trial patient matching is inherently demographic in nature, so residual demographic disparity cannot be eliminated without compromising the scientific validity of the trial.
options.D: Debiasing on explicit demographic variables does not eliminate bias that is encoded in proxy variables — other features correlated with demographics that were not included in the retraining procedure.

items.question:
A credit union member is denied an unsecured personal loan. They write to the credit union requesting an explanation of the AI-assisted denial. The compliance officer sends the member a copy of the internal audit log, which records the model's input variables and output score. The member replies that this does not help them understand why they were denied.

What distinction is the member MOST likely pointing to?

options.A: The audit log documents what data the model processed; a meaningful explanation translates this into the specific reasons for the denial in terms the individual can understand and potentially act upon.
options.B: The member is only entitled to a full explanation if the AI made the final decision independently, without any human review.
options.C: The audit log satisfies the technical explanation requirement; the member's further request is actually for an appeal, which is a separate process.
options.D: Providing the audit log to the member creates a data-protection risk because it reveals model structure the credit union considers commercially sensitive.

items.question:
A telecoms company is developing an AI use policy and is debating when disclosure of AI involvement is required. Two scenarios are raised: (1) a Claude-generated internal briefing note summarising a team meeting for the attending managers; (2) a customer-facing monthly bill insert generated by Claude explaining a new pricing structure to 400,000 subscribers.

For which scenario is an AI disclosure obligation MOST clearly warranted?

options.A: For the internal briefing note, because employees deserve to know when AI generated a summary they may rely on for decision-making.
options.B: For the customer-facing bill insert, because it is a consequential external communication directed at individuals who have no visibility into how it was produced.
options.C: For both, because any use of AI in business communication should be disclosed to all recipients regardless of audience or purpose.
options.D: For neither, because disclosure is only required when AI was directly involved in a regulated financial or legal decision, not in routine operational communications.

items.question:
A university admissions office uses Claude to produce a standardised score for each applicant's personal statement as one of four components in a holistic review. The final admissions decision is made by a human officer. A faculty governance committee argues this is high-stakes AI use requiring additional oversight; the admissions director argues it is a consistency tool for processing high volume.

Which consideration should MOST influence the governance committee's assessment?

options.A: The number of applicants affected — a process touching 4,000 applicants has greater aggregate impact and automatically meets the high-stakes threshold.
options.B: The consistency benefit — if AI reduces scoring variance across reviewers, it increases fairness and reduces the need for additional oversight.
options.C: Whether the AI score systematically influences outcomes for certain applicant groups — if it does, the high-stakes threshold is met regardless of the human review layer.
options.D: Whether applicants are informed that AI is used in scoring, because disclosure shifts the accountability burden from the institution to applicants who choose to proceed.

items.question:
A fintech company is designing a human-in-the-loop step for its AI-assisted KYC verification process. The compliance director wants to ensure the human review step constitutes genuine oversight, not a nominal approval process. Two design features would most directly achieve this.

Which TWO features distinguish genuine oversight from nominal review? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Reviewers must access and assess the underlying source documents for each case, not only the AI-generated summary.
options.B: Reviewers receive a confidence score alongside each AI recommendation, enabling proportional calibration of review intensity.
options.C: The review step is positioned before the decision is communicated to the applicant, not as a post-hoc audit of automated decisions already sent.
options.D: A daily cap on the number of cases any single reviewer handles limits the volume-driven pressure that produces rubber-stamping.
options.E: A second AI model cross-checks the primary model's output, providing the human reviewer with two independent AI assessments for each case.

items.question:
A consumer insurance company has updated its AI pricing model and the data science team has completed a technical bias-mitigation pass. A risk committee member argues two additional governance steps are required before the updated model is used for live pricing decisions.

Which TWO governance steps are required before live deployment? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The data science team should run a second iteration of technical bias mitigation to validate that the first pass was sufficient.
options.B: An independent assessment of pricing fairness outcomes, tested on actual historical customer cohorts across demographic groups, must be completed before live deployment.
options.C: The model's training data should be archived and made available to regulators on request, in anticipation of potential future scrutiny of the mitigation approach.
options.D: A defined process for investigating and responding to individual customer pricing fairness complaints must be in place before the model goes live.
options.E: The actuarial team must certify that the bias-mitigation changes did not reduce the model's overall predictive accuracy below acceptable thresholds.

items.question:
A legal technology company provides AI-assisted contract review to corporate clients. The product manager must clearly define what the AI component can and cannot do, so that clients understand where AI stops and qualified legal judgment must begin. Two statements accurately describe this boundary.

Which TWO statements accurately describe the boundary? (Choose TWO)

options.A: AI contract review can identify clauses that deviate from market-standard language and flag them for lawyer review; it cannot determine whether a deviation is commercially acceptable for a specific client's circumstances.
options.B: AI contract review can replace lawyer review for standard commercial contracts below a defined transaction-value threshold, because low-value contracts pose low legal risk.
options.C: AI contract review can produce risk scores for identified clauses; the weight to give each risk in a negotiation strategy requires legal and commercial judgment the client's lawyer must provide.
options.D: The lawyer retains professional responsibility for advice given, regardless of how extensively AI tools were used to analyse the contract.
options.E: AI contract review eliminates the need for a lawyer to read the full contract; only AI-flagged clauses require lawyer attention.

items.question:
An international retailer plans to deploy an AI system that will screen 3,000 job applicants and automatically advance or reject them before any human reviews individual applications. The legal team must identify the two obligations that must be met before the system goes live.

Which TWO obligations must be met before deployment? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Applicants must be given the option to opt into AI screening before submitting their application, under an explicit opt-in consent model.
options.B: Applicants must be informed, before they submit their application, that an automated system will make the initial screening decision about their candidacy.
options.C: Applicants must be told what categories of data the AI system will assess and how those data will influence the automated screening outcome.
options.D: The AI screening system must complete a minimum 90-day human-reviewed pilot before any automated rejection decisions are sent to applicants.
options.E: The retailer must publish its complete AI screening methodology as a publicly accessible document so all potential applicants can review the process before applying.

items.question:
An AI-assisted HR system has flagged an employee for termination review after detecting performance patterns consistent with the company's severance criteria. The HR director has received the flag and is planning next steps. Steps completed so far: the AI flag has been noted; the HR director has read a one-paragraph summary of the termination criteria; the employee has not been informed. The HR director must now decide what to do NEXT.

What should the HR director do NEXT?

options.A: Inform the employee immediately that a termination review is under way, so they have maximum opportunity to provide context before any decision is made.
options.B: Refer the case to external employment law counsel to obtain a legal opinion on whether the AI-identified patterns satisfy the contractual termination criteria.
options.C: Escalate the case to the CHRO and legal department so that the decision is not taken by a single HR director without organisational sign-off.
options.D: Conduct an independent substantive review of the specific performance evidence underlying the AI flag, assessing whether the evidence actually supports the termination criteria.

items.question:
A junior analyst joins an investment bank's M&A advisory team. The team maintains a Claude Project containing live deal term sheets, client financial models, and confidential negotiation notes for six active transactions. The team lead asks how Project access should be configured for the new hire.

What is the MOST appropriate approach?

options.A: Grant access only to team members whose roles require the deal information, scoped to the transactions they are actively working on
options.B: Share the Project link with the broader research department so analysts can use the embedded templates
options.C: Archive the confidential documents and create a sanitised version of the Project for wider distribution
options.D: Grant the junior analyst access to all team Projects immediately to accelerate their onboarding ramp

items.question:
An HR business partner at a 4,000-person manufacturing firm maintains a Claude Project containing current salary bands, performance improvement plan templates, and termination checklists. She wants to share the Project with all 200 line managers so they can generate review-preparation notes.

Which access design is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Grant all 4,000 employees read access so the compensation structure is transparent organisation-wide
options.B: Limit Project access to HR staff and the specific managers who directly conduct performance reviews
options.C: Make the salary band documents publicly accessible internally and restrict only the termination checklists
options.D: Move salary data to a separate Project and share a templates-only Project with all 200 managers

items.question:
A biotech startup's compliance officer asks the AI programme team why they have configured export logging for every Claude conversation in their enterprise deployment. The team lead says it is 'standard practice' but cannot articulate the specific rationale.

What is the PRIMARY governance purpose of maintaining these conversation logs?

options.A: To feed conversation data back to Anthropic so that Claude's responses improve for the company's specific use cases
options.B: To measure individual employee productivity by tracking how frequently each person uses Claude
options.C: To create a traceable record so that outputs and the context that produced them can be reviewed if challenged
options.D: To enable automatic deletion of conversations containing personally identifiable information after a set retention period

items.question:
A loan officer at a regional bank uses Claude to help draft adverse action notices — letters informing applicants that their loan application was declined. His manager asks whether the AI-generated drafts and subsequent edits, prior to sending, need to be retained in the bank's document management system.

What is the MAIN reason to retain both the draft and the final sent version?

options.A: To demonstrate compliance with Anthropic's enterprise data retention guidelines for financial institutions
options.B: To build a future training dataset from the loan officer's edits to improve AI-generated letters over time
options.C: To track which loan officers relied on AI assistance for performance management purposes
options.D: To ensure the content of credit decisions can be reviewed, explained, and audited if an applicant challenges the notice

items.question:
A product manager at a 300-person SaaS company has built a Claude Project containing six competitive intelligence reports and an unreleased pricing strategy document. She wants to share the Project with the 12-person product team before an upcoming planning session. (Choose TWO)

Which TWO controls should she implement BEFORE sharing access?

options.A: Restrict Project membership to the product team members whose roles require the competitive and pricing data
options.B: Export all documents to a shared drive so that access management is handled outside the AI tool
options.C: Review each document in the Project and remove or separately protect any content not appropriate for all intended recipients
options.D: Notify all company employees that the Project exists so anyone who finds it relevant can request access
options.E: Move the Project to a personal account to simplify sharing without triggering IT governance requirements

items.question:
During an IT audit at a 15,000-person insurance company, auditors discover that a group of claims adjusters has been using a free public AI chatbot to summarise claim reports and draft coverage assessments. The company has an approved enterprise AI tool, a data governance policy, and an acceptable-use policy — none of which the adjusters followed.

Which term BEST describes this behaviour from a governance standpoint?

options.A: AI misuse, because employees used an AI tool for tasks outside their job descriptions
options.B: Shadow AI, because employees used unapproved AI tools outside IT governance and policy controls
options.C: Unauthorised processing, because the term specifically covers sharing data with third parties without an agreement
options.D: Data exfiltration, because employees deliberately sent sensitive claim data to an external service

items.question:
A CTO at an 80-person software startup learns that engineers have been pasting code snippets — including database schema files and functions containing live internal API keys — into a public AI chatbot for debugging help. No data-sharing agreement exists with the chatbot provider.

What is the MOST significant risk created by this behaviour?

options.A: The engineers may receive lower-quality debugging suggestions than a purpose-built development tool would provide
options.B: The startup may inadvertently violate open-source licence terms if the AI was trained on GPL-licensed code
options.C: Confidential source code and live credentials may be exposed to a third-party service with unknown data retention practices
options.D: Engineers gain an unfair productivity advantage over colleagues who are not using AI assistance

items.question:
An IT security team at a 2,000-person logistics company wants to identify whether employees are using unapproved AI services on corporate devices, despite a company policy requiring prior approval for all external AI tools. The team has standard enterprise monitoring capabilities.

Which detection method is MOST directly useful?

options.A: Reviewing network traffic logs for outbound connections to known AI service domains and endpoints
options.B: Surveying employees anonymously about their AI usage habits and taking self-reported responses at face value
options.C: Comparing employee productivity metrics before and after the policy was issued to infer which teams may be using AI
options.D: Requiring employees to submit an annual IT asset declaration listing all software installed on their devices

items.question:
A global retailer's internal audit team reviews how the merchandise planning department uses Claude to generate initial inventory allocation recommendations. Planners accept or override the AI recommendations, but the audit team finds that no record is made of whether human review occurred before each recommendation is acted upon in the purchasing system.

What is the PRIMARY audit concern raised by this finding?

options.A: Planners may be using a model tier that is not powerful enough for inventory optimisation work
options.B: The AI tool lacks an approved integration with the purchasing system's approval workflow
options.C: Claude may produce different recommendations for identical inputs across runs, undermining planning consistency
options.D: There is no traceable record of whether a human reviewed AI output before a business decision was implemented

items.question:
A compliance analyst at a large telecom company is designing an audit logging standard for all Claude deployments across the enterprise. The standard must satisfy both internal audit requirements and external regulatory expectations for the company's licensed communications business. (Choose TWO)

Which TWO elements are MOST essential in every conversation log entry?

options.A: The exact model version and API endpoint used for each conversation
options.B: The identity of the user who submitted the prompt, tied to an authoritative directory with a timestamp
options.C: The number of tokens consumed in each turn so that cost allocation reports can be produced
options.D: A reference sufficient to retrieve the full output content if a specific conversation is later reviewed
options.E: A list of all other users who viewed the same Project during the same calendar month

items.question:
A legal counsel at a 60-person professional services firm drafts the company's first AI acceptable-use policy. Once approved, the managing partner asks whether employees need formal training on the policy or whether distributing the document by email is sufficient.

What is the MOST appropriate answer?

options.A: Email distribution is sufficient because the policy document itself is the authoritative reference employees can consult
options.B: Training is only necessary for employees whose roles involve regulated data or client-facing deliverables
options.C: Formal training with documented completion records is more effective than email alone, especially for a policy with compliance implications
options.D: Training is only needed if the firm chooses to activate enforcement; communication requirements and enforcement requirements are separate

items.question:
A content writer at a 15-person marketing agency uses Claude to produce first-draft copy for a client's product launch campaign. The agency wants to assign copyright in the final copy to the client under their standard work-for-hire agreement. A colleague argues that AI involvement means copyright cannot be assigned because the content was not created by a human.

What is the MOST accurate governance position the agency should take?

options.A: Document the human creative direction, selection, and editing that shaped the final copy, and rely on that contribution as the basis for copyright
options.B: Disclose AI involvement to the client and treat the content as entirely public domain with no copyright protections
options.C: Register the copyright jointly in the names of the agency and Anthropic, reflecting shared authorship of the work
options.D: Cease using AI tools for client deliverables until clear legal standards on AI copyright are established in every relevant jurisdiction

items.question:
A security analyst at a mid-market financial services firm explains to her team why their Claude deployment should not directly summarise emails flagged as potential phishing attempts without any content filtering or sandboxing. A colleague argues that Claude is 'just reading' the email, so there is no real risk.

What risk is the analyst MOST likely trying to prevent?

options.A: Claude may produce an output that is too long and difficult to parse because phishing emails are often verbose
options.B: A malicious actor could embed instructions in the email content that attempt to manipulate Claude's behaviour during processing
options.C: The email might contain copyrighted content that Claude would reproduce, creating an intellectual property risk
options.D: Processing suspected phishing emails may cause Claude to permanently learn and replicate malicious patterns in future responses

items.question:
A nurse manager at a large hospital discovers that a nursing aide used Claude to draft a patient medication summary that was included in a handoff note without clinical review. The summary contained an incorrect dosage for one medication. A pharmacist caught the error before administration. The incident must now be formally managed. (Choose TWO)

Which TWO actions represent the MOST important FIRST steps?

options.A: Document the incident in the hospital's patient safety reporting system with a full account of the error and how it was caught
options.B: Immediately suspend all AI tool use across the entire hospital pending a complete organisational review
options.C: Check whether similar unchecked AI-generated summaries appeared in other recent handoff notes that may not have been caught
options.D: Notify Anthropic of the clinical error so the model can be retrained to avoid similar mistakes
options.E: Issue a public statement disclosing the near-miss event to patients and their families without delay

items.question:
A procurement director at a large energy company is evaluating a new AI-powered contract analytics vendor. She has confirmed the vendor uses Claude's API as its underlying model and has received the vendor's completed security questionnaire responses. She is now preparing a risk recommendation for the IT governance committee.

What should she do NEXT to complete an adequate vendor risk assessment?

options.A: Issue the contract immediately since the vendor uses a reputable AI model from an established provider
options.B: Ask the IT team to conduct penetration testing for prompt injection vulnerabilities in a sandboxed environment
options.C: Request the vendor's sub-processor list to understand whether customer contract data flows to any additional third parties
options.D: Review the vendor's data processing agreement to confirm how customer data is handled, retained, and deleted

items.question:
A CIO at a 900-person professional services firm is initiating a formal procurement review for an AI writing assistant that the proposals team has requested. The tool will process client RFP content and internal proposal drafts. The CIO wants to structure the review correctly from the outset.

What is the MOST appropriate FIRST step in the procurement process?

options.A: Approve the tool conditionally with a 90-day pilot period before conducting any security or data governance review
options.B: Ask the proposals team to conduct a hands-on evaluation and report back on whether the tool is useful
options.C: Define the data handling, security, and compliance criteria the tool must meet before beginning vendor evaluation
options.D: Request pricing from at least three competing vendors so cost comparison can anchor the procurement decision

items.question:
A policy manager at a large pharmaceutical company has drafted an AI acceptable-use policy that prohibits uploading unpublished clinical trial data to any external AI service. A research lead requests an exception, arguing that a specific vendor tool would significantly speed up a study report due in 60 days. There is no formal exception process in the policy.

What should the policy manager do FIRST?

options.A: Establish a formal written exception process with defined criteria, an approval authority, a risk review requirement, and a time limit before evaluating this specific request
options.B: Deny the exception request because the policy states no unpublished clinical data may be uploaded to external AI services
options.C: Grant the exception verbally for 60 days since the deadline creates a legitimate business justification
options.D: Escalate the request to the chief medical officer without a recommendation, as clinical data decisions are outside policy scope

items.question:
A marketing director at a major retail chain notices that her team of 30 is regularly using a consumer AI chatbot for campaign copywriting despite the company's approved enterprise AI tool being available. When she surveys the team informally, members say the approved tool is 'too slow' and the approval process to access it 'takes weeks.'

What does this scenario MOST clearly indicate about the root cause of shadow AI use?

options.A: The team lacks awareness that using the consumer tool violates the acceptable-use policy
options.B: The approved tool's usability and access friction are driving employees toward the unapproved alternative
options.C: The marketing director has failed to enforce the acceptable-use policy and should be disciplined
options.D: Consumer AI tools are inherently better suited to creative tasks than enterprise AI tools

items.question:
A software development lead at a FinTech startup uses Claude to review pull request descriptions and generate release notes from commit messages. The startup has no formal AI policy. A new security-focused board member asks whether this usage requires any governance oversight.

What is the MOST appropriate response from the CTO?

options.A: No oversight is needed because Claude is only reading commit messages, not executing code or accessing production systems
options.B: Oversight is optional because the startup's small size makes formal AI governance disproportionate to the risk
options.C: Oversight is recommended but only if the startup processes payment card data, which would trigger PCI requirements
options.D: The usage should be formally reviewed because commit messages and pull request descriptions may contain sensitive architecture or credential information

items.question:
An HR director at a 5,000-person global professional services firm discovers widespread shadow AI use after an IT audit reveals connections to at least four unapproved consumer AI services from corporate devices. She is designing a response programme. (Choose TWO)

Which TWO responses address the ROOT CAUSES of shadow AI use most effectively?

options.A: Issue an immediate disciplinary warning to all employees whose devices appeared in the network logs
options.B: Block all outbound connections to known consumer AI services at the network level
options.C: Survey employees to understand what tasks they are using unapproved tools for and what gaps the approved tools do not fill
options.D: Accelerate provisioning of the approved enterprise AI tool and streamline the access request process
options.E: Circulate a reminder of the acceptable-use policy with a deadline for employees to certify they have read it

items.question:
A compliance officer at a large insurance company is reviewing the company's AI acceptable-use policy, which was written two years ago and covers only 'automated decision systems.' A senior underwriter points out that she uses Claude for draft policy wordings and risk summaries, and asks whether she is subject to the policy.

What should the compliance officer conclude?

options.A: The underwriter is subject to the policy because Claude is an AI tool used in business processes, regardless of whether it makes final decisions
options.B: The underwriter is not subject to the policy because Claude produces drafts for human review rather than making automated decisions
options.C: The underwriter is subject to the policy only if the draft wordings are sent directly to policyholders without additional editing
options.D: The policy does not apply because the underwriter uses Claude interactively rather than in an automated pipeline

items.question:
A technical writer at a gaming company uses Claude to help draft user manual sections. The company's legal team asks whether AI-generated portions of the manual can be registered for copyright protection in the same way as the human-authored sections.

What is the MOST accurate guidance the legal team should give?

options.A: Yes — any output produced by a licensed AI tool is automatically assigned to the tool's licensee for copyright purposes
options.B: Sections where a human provided significant creative direction and editorial selection are more likely to support a copyright claim than purely AI-generated passages
options.C: No — any document containing AI-generated text loses copyright protection for the entire work, including the human-authored portions
options.D: Yes — copyright registration is always granted for commercial products regardless of how the content was produced

items.question:
A brand manager at a consumer goods company asks Claude to generate a jingle for a new product, specifying only the product name and target audience. The resulting jingle sounds melodically similar to a well-known advertising jingle from a competitor. The brand manager's colleague says this is fine because AI-generated content is automatically original.

What governance concern does this situation MOST clearly illustrate?

options.A: Claude is producing outputs that are longer than necessary, making the jingle difficult to use in standard advertising slots
options.B: The brand manager should have used a higher-capability model to ensure greater stylistic originality
options.C: AI-generated content may reflect patterns from training data and should be reviewed for similarity to existing copyrighted works before commercial use
options.D: The colleague is correct because AI-generated content is always original by definition and cannot infringe copyright

items.question:
A sell-side analyst at a mid-size brokerage asks Claude to draft a competitive landscape section for a client pitch. The output includes: "According to a 2024 McKinsey Global Institute report, 61% of asset managers plan to double their quantitative headcount by 2026." The analyst searches McKinsey's publications site and finds no report by that name or statistic.

What is the MOST likely explanation?

options.A: Claude generated a plausible-sounding citation that does not correspond to any real publication.
options.B: The report exists but is paywalled and therefore absent from public search indexes.
options.C: Claude's training data predates the 2024 publication, so it referenced an earlier edition under the wrong title.
options.D: The statistic is real but Claude misattributed it to McKinsey rather than the original research firm.

items.question:
A clinical informatics manager at a regional hospital asks Claude to summarise approved indications for a recently licensed biosimilar. The response lists several real indications correctly but also states the drug is approved for a specific paediatric inflammatory condition the manager cannot locate in any regulatory database or prescribing information.

Which approach BEST distinguishes whether this is a knowledge-cutoff error or a fabrication?

options.A: Resubmit the prompt to a higher-tier model to obtain a more accurate answer for clinical queries.
options.B: Search a regulatory database to determine whether the indication was approved before the training cutoff, after it, or never submitted.
options.C: Treat the error as a cutoff gap and revisit the indication when the next model version is released.
options.D: Compare results across two separate Claude conversations and accept the answer that appears in both.
